subtopics.title: Resultants, Tail-to-Head and the Closed Diagram

questions.question: The resultant of two or more vectors is best defined as:
options: The largest of the vectors being added
The single vector that has the same effect as all of them acting together
The sum of their magnitudes only
The difference between the biggest and smallest vector

questions.question: In the tail-to-head method, the resultant is the arrow drawn from:
options: The tail of the first vector to the head of the last vector
The head of the first vector to the tail of the last vector
The midpoint of one vector to the midpoint of the other
The head of the largest vector to the origin

questions.question: Three forces drawn tail-to-head form a CLOSED vector diagram. This tells you that:
options: The forces are all equal in magnitude
The object must be moving at increasing speed
The resultant is zero and the object is in equilibrium
One force is twice the size of the other two

questions.question: The equilibrant of a set of forces is:
options: Half the resultant, in the same direction
The vertical component of the resultant
Equal in magnitude to the resultant but opposite in direction

subtopics.title: Resolving a Vector into Perpendicular Components

questions.question: For a vector R at angle θ measured from the x-axis, the components are:
options: Rx = R sinθ and Ry = R cosθ
Rx = R cosθ and Ry = R sinθ
Rx = R tanθ and Ry = R cosθ

questions.question: The safest rule for deciding between sine and cosine when resolving is:
options: The component adjacent to the marked angle uses cosine; the component opposite it uses sine
Always use cosine for the horizontal component, whatever the angle is measured from
Use sine when the force is large and cosine when it is small
Use whichever gives the bigger answer

questions.question: A 250 N cable pulls at 30° above the horizontal. Its horizontal component is:
Taking east and north as positive, a 120 N force due west is written as:

subtopics.title: Adding the Components of Four Forces

questions.question: When adding vectors by components, you may:
options: Add x-components to y-components as long as the units match
Add all x-components together and all y-components together, separately
Add the magnitudes of all the vectors directly

questions.question: For the four workshop forces (250 N at 30°, 180 N north, 120 N west, 90 N south), Rx equals:
For the same four forces, Ry equals:
Why should you write "x = 0" for a force pointing due north instead of leaving it out?
options: Because a northward force secretly has a small eastward part
Because the marker awards a mark for the number zero itself
Because it changes the value of Ry
Because it proves the vector was resolved and not simply forgotten

subtopics.title: Magnitude by Pythagoras, Direction by Trigonometry

questions.question: With Rx = 96,5 N and Ry = 215 N, the magnitude of the resultant is:
The direction of that resultant is found from:
options: θ = tan⁻¹(Ry ÷ Rx) = tan⁻¹(2,228) = 65,8° north of east
θ = sin⁻¹(Rx ÷ Ry) = 26,6° east of north

questions.question: A learner's inverse tangent returns 1,15 instead of 65,8. The most likely cause is:
options: The calculator is in radian mode instead of degree mode
The square root was not taken

questions.question: A displacement of 60 m east followed by 80 m north gives a resultant of:

subtopics.title: Walking to the Shop the Long Way

questions.question: You walk 60 m east then 80 m north. The distance walked and the resultant displacement are:
Walking north first and east second instead of east first and north second changes:
options: Nothing about the resultant — you land on the same corner
Both the magnitude and the direction

questions.question: If a series of trips brings you back to your own gate, then in physics terms:
options: The forces are all zero individually
The resultant has no length — the forces cancel and the object is in equilibrium
The object must be accelerating uniformly

subtopics.title: Splitting One Push into Two Honest Pushes

questions.question: A suitcase handle is pulled at a tilt. Splitting that pull into a forward part and an upward part means:
options: The pull has been made bigger
Some of the pull has been lost
There are now two extra forces on the suitcase
The same pull has simply been sorted into two perpendicular parts

questions.question: A pull tilted almost straight up will have:
options: A large upward part and a small forward part
A large forward part and a small upward part

questions.question: The upward part of a 250 N pull tilted 30° above the ground is:
In the sorting rule, the side of the triangle lying next to the marked angle uses:
Adding the sideways parts 216,5 east and 120 west gives:
Adding the upward parts 125 north, 180 north and 90 south gives:
Handing in "235,7 N" with no direction is a problem because:
options: The number is wrong without the direction
Newtons are not the correct unit for a resultant
The direction is only needed for displacement, not force
A vector answer is incomplete without a direction, and the marker will award only part of the marks

questions.question: The three moves of the component method, in order, are:
options: Draw to scale, measure with a ruler, convert units
Split every vector into two parts, add each part separately, rebuild one arrow with Pythagoras and inverse tangent
Add all magnitudes, divide by the number of vectors, state the average direction
Find the biggest vector, subtract the rest, state the remainder
